subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me a challenging GCSE exam-style question on binary, denary and hexadecimal number conversions, then mark my answer against the CCEA spec.
promptWeak: Explain how binary, denary and hexadecimal number conversions work for GCSE CCEA Computer Science simply, with an example and the most common mistake.

questions.q: How many different symbols (digits) are used in the binary number system?
questions.explain: Binary is a base-2 system, so it uses only two symbols: 0 and 1.

questions.q: How many bits are there in one byte?
questions.explain: A byte is made up of 8 bits. Each bit is a single binary digit (0 or 1).

questions.q: What is the 8-bit binary number 00101101 in denary?
questions.explain: Place values with a 1 are 32 + 8 + 4 + 1 = 45.

questions.q: What is the denary number 100 as an 8-bit binary number?
questions.explain: 100 = 64 + 32 + 4, so the bits set are 64, 32 and 4, giving 01100100.

questions.q: What is the largest denary value that can be stored in 8 bits?
questions.explain: 8 bits can store 2^8 = 256 different values, from 0 to 255, so the largest is 255.

questions.q: The hexadecimal system is base 16. Which set of symbols does it use?
questions.explain: Hexadecimal uses the ten digits 0-9 plus six letters A-F (representing 10-15), giving 16 symbols.

questions.q: What is the hexadecimal number 2F in denary?
questions.explain: 2F = (2 x 16) + 15 = 32 + 15 = 47. F represents 15 in hexadecimal.

questions.q: What is the binary number 11010110 written in hexadecimal?
questions.explain: Split into nibbles: 1101 = D and 0110 = 6, giving D6.

questions.q: How many binary bits can a single hexadecimal digit represent?
questions.explain: One hexadecimal digit represents exactly 4 binary bits (a nibble), because 16 = 2^4.

questions.q: What is the denary number 200 in hexadecimal?
questions.explain: 200 / 16 = 12 remainder 8. 12 is C in hex, so 200 = C8.

questions.q: Which list places the data units in order from smallest to largest?
questions.explain: A bit is smallest, then a byte (8 bits), then kilobyte, then megabyte.

questions.q: What is a character set such as ASCII used to represent?
questions.explain: A character set maps each text character (letters, digits, symbols) to a unique binary code so text can be stored digitally.

questions.q: What is the main advantage of Unicode over standard ASCII?
options: It can represent characters from many more languages and symbols
It uses fewer bits per character
questions.explain: Unicode uses more bits per character, allowing it to represent characters and symbols from many languages worldwide, far beyond ASCII's limited set.

questions.q: In a bitmap image, what is each individual dot of colour called?
questions.explain: A bitmap image is made up of pixels (picture elements), each storing a binary code for its colour.

questions.q: An image uses a colour depth of 4 bits per pixel. How many different colours can each pixel display?
questions.explain: The number of colours = 2^(colour depth) = 2^4 = 16 colours.

questions.q: Increasing the resolution of an image (more pixels) will generally have what effect?
options: Have no effect on file size
Reduce file size but increase detail
questions.explain: More pixels means more detail, but each pixel must be stored, so the file size increases.

questions.q: How is analogue sound converted into digital data?
options: By taking regular samples of the sound wave's amplitude
questions.explain: Sound is digitised by sampling: measuring the amplitude of the sound wave at frequent, regular intervals and storing each as binary.

questions.q: What happens to sound quality and file size when the sample rate is increased?
questions.explain: A higher sample rate takes more samples per second, so the recording is truer to the original (higher quality) but the file size increases.

questions.q: Which statement about lossless compression is correct?
options: It is only used for video
The original data can be perfectly reconstructed
questions.explain: Lossless compression reduces file size in a way that allows the exact original data to be restored, with no loss of information.

questions.q: Why is lossy compression often acceptable for photos and music but not for text documents?
options: Text cannot be compressed at all
Small losses of detail are usually unnoticeable in images and audio, but text must stay exact
Lossy compression cannot be used on images
questions.explain: Lossy compression discards some data; a small quality loss is often unnoticeable in photos or audio, but losing characters in text would corrupt its meaning.
